title: Stock Status of Ompok bimaculatus in Kaptai Lake: A Length‐Based Approach for Sustainable Fisheries Management
content:
ABSTRACT

Ompok bimaculatus, a silurid catfish, is a commercially valuable and endangered species in Bangladesh. Kaptai Lake is a critical habitat for this species, yet growing market demand and ecological pressures jeopardize stock sustainability. Therefore, this study employed a length-based approach integrating LB-SPR and aLBI to conduct the baseline stock assessment of the species in the lake. The LB-SPR suggests that the stock may be experiencing overfishing with a reduced spawning potential ratio (SPR = 0.30) and unsustainable fishing pressure (F/M = 1.32). Furthermore, the length at 50% selectivity (SL 50 = 19.67 cm) fell below the length at 50% maturity (L 50 = 21.02 cm), indicating potential growth overfishing. The aLBI model estimated the key length parameters: asymptotic length (L ∞ = 36.32 cm), length at maturity (L mat = 21.04 cm) and optimum length (L opt = 21.72 cm). The percentage of mature fish (P mat = 65.03%) and the percentage of optimally sized fish (P opt = 42.49%) fell short of the target of 100%. The percentage of mega-spawners (P mega = 31.78%) exceeding 20% suggests potential recruitment overfishing. In addition, the probability of stock biomass being below the target (TSB40) and limit reference points (LSB25) was 100%, remaining completely stable across ±5% and ±10% parameter variations (L ∞ and L mat) before exhibiting dynamic shifts at ±15%. Based on these findings, this study recommends implementing a length range between L opt and L opt + 10% of L opt to protect juveniles and mega-spawners. Finally, addressing the underlying drivers of overfishing to reduce F/M is essential.
